nl.statement: An adaptive multi-arm causal experiment at horizon \(T\): a probability space carrying a filtration \(\mathcal F_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\mathcal F_T\); independent and identically distributed full-data draws \(W_t=(X_t,(Y_t(a))_{a\in\mathcal A})\) on a measurable context space \(\mathcal X\) with finite action set \(\mathcal A=\{1,\ldots,K\}\); a measurable policy map \(\Pi:\mathcal A\times\mathcal X\times\mathsf H\to[0,1]\) whose arm probabilities sum to one, driven by a predictable policy state \(\eta_{t}\in\mathsf H\subset\mathbb R^q\); randomized actions \(A_t\) drawn from \(\pi_t(\cdot\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})=\Pi(\cdot\mid X_t,\eta_{t-1})\) conditionally independently of \((Y_t(a))_{a\in\mathcal A}\); observed outcomes \(Y_t=Y_t(A_t)\); a stacked causal score \(g(a,x,y;\theta)\in\mathbb R^d\) on a compact \(\Theta\subset\mathbb R^d\), with population moment \(M_P\), distinguished root \(\theta^*\), Jacobian \(H\), adaptive IPW scores \(\xi_t\), cumulative score \(S_T\), predictable and realized quadratic variations \(\langle S\rangle_T\) and \([S]_T\), the state-indexed score covariance \(\Gamma_P\), and the standard normal law \(\Phi\) used by every Wald statement. — New `AdaptiveCausalExperiment` structure (planned in `Basic.lean`): filtration + i.i.d. full data + predictable `Fin K`-valued policy + potential outcomes + score. Partial fit only, so bypass-justified: the K-arm policy-state world is a strict generalization; the binary structure is reused in S2 as a ROW-INDEXED FAMILY (`row : ℕ → AdaptiveExperiment Omega m0`, one library experiment per triangular-array row) and the overlap idiom is copied -- copied, not called: per the round-6 fix the S2 class field is the local ALMOST-EVERYWHERE predicate `RowOverlapAE`, since the library's `HasOverlap` bounds the propensity at every `omega` whereas the source condition is almost sure. Causalean's `Experimentation/DesignBased/` cluster is finite-population `FiniteDesign` (finite Omega, `E X = sum p z * X z`) and cannot express a filtration, `condExp`, or a superpopulation martingale; `htTotal/htMean/htEffect/E_htEffect/var_htMean_le/Exposure.*/PotentialOutcome.*/chebyshev/EdgeVarianceBound.*/Var_prod_linear_comb/E_compound_tower/Var_compound_eq_tower/IndepSummandsCLT.*/DepGraphCLT.*/LocalDependenceCLT.*` from the supplied reuse list are all `FiniteDesign`-typed and therefore bypass-justified at the wrong abstraction. The binary-treatment triangular array of AIPW adaptive experiments: for each row \(n\), independent and identically distributed full-data triples \((X_{n,t},Y_{n,t}(0),Y_{n,t}(1))\) unaffected by the policy, a pre-treatment \(\sigma\)-field \(\mathcal B_{n,t}\) containing the past and the current covariate, a logged predictable propensity \(\pi_{n,t}\) with \(\mathbb P_n(A_{n,t}=1\mid\mathcal B_{n,t})=\pi_{n,t}\) and, almost surely at every scored index \(t\in\mathcal T_n\), \(\epsilon\le\pi_{n,t}\le1-\epsilon\), consistency \(Y_{n,t}=A_{n,t}Y_{n,t}(1)+(1-A_{n,t})Y_{n,t}(0)\), history-measurable regressions \(\widehat m_{n,t-1,a}\), a deterministic scored set \(\mathcal T_n\) of size \(N_n\), the AIPW pseudo-outcome \(\widehat\phi_{n,t}\) with target \(\theta_{0,n}=E\{Y_{n,t}(1)-Y_{n,t}(0)\}\), and the scored-order filtration \(\mathcal G_{n,s}\). Only fourth-moment envelopes on outcomes and fitted regressions are imposed; no almost-sure bound on the centered scores. — REVISED (round 4): the carrier is now at the RIGHT ARITY for the triangular array. The round-3 plan gave `SacoArrayWorld` a single field `base : AdaptiveExperiment Omega m0`, which is an arity error the reviewer correctly flagged: the library decl carries exactly ONE filtration `ℱ : Filtration ℕ m0` and ONE propensity process `propensity : ℕ → Ω → ℝ` (signature re-read at `Causalean/Experimentation/Sequential/AdaptiveDesign.lean:48-61`), so a single `base` cannot host the row-indexed family `pi_{n,t}` nor the row filtrations `F_{n,·}`. FIX: the design layer is a ROW-INDEXED FAMILY of library experiments, `structure SacoArrayWorld (Omega : Type*) (m0 : MeasurableSpace Omega) where row : ℕ → Causalean.Experimentation.Sequential.AdaptiveExperiment Omega m0` (emitted in the run's Lean target subdirectory, `.../Research/Saco/World.lean`; NOT the library decl). Two defects are fixed together. (b) DOMAIN. This a.e. shape is the library's own idiom for a source-faithful overlap condition: `Causalean.Estimation.ATE.Score.AIPWMoment.H_ε_aeL2` (AIPWMoment.lean:302-306) is the source-shaped a.e./L2 nuisance set `{eta | (∀ᵐ x ∂P_X, eps ≤ eta.e_fn x ∧ eta.e_fn x ≤ 1 - eps) ∧ ...}` and is explicitly contrasted in that file's own docstring with the legacy POINTWISE overlap-bounded realization set `H_ε` -- the same pointwise-vs-a.e. distinction, resolved the same way. The library `HasOverlap` is RETAINED (still in `reuse_ingredients`) but only on the WITNESS side, through a one-way bridge lemma proved locally in `Saco/World.lean`, `lemma rowOverlapAE_of_hasOverlap {W : SacoArrayWorld Omega 𝒳} {eps : ℝ} (heps : eps < 1/2) (h : forall n, AdaptiveExperiment.HasOverlap (W.row n) eps) : RowOverlapAE W eps` -- it discards BOTH strengthenings at once, weakening the pointwise bound to an a.e. one by `Filter.Eventually.of_forall` and restricting the `forall t` to `t ∈ W.scoredSet n` by simply dropping the membership hypothesis. The parent decl hosts NONE of the following, which are therefore ADDITIONAL local fields of `SacoArrayWorld`, each stated against the row-specific design layer `W.row n`: (1) row-indexed full data / potential outcomes `X : ℕ → ℕ → Ω → 𝒳`, `Y0 Y1 : ℕ → ℕ → Ω → ℝ` (row `n`, occasion `t`) with the i.i.d.-within-row / policy-unaffected field (Assumptions 3.5-3.6); (2) the row-indexed assignment process `A : ℕ → ℕ → Ω → ℝ` valued in `{0,1}`; (3) the consistency link `Y = A * Y1 + (1 - A) * Y0` a.s. The bounded-noise clipped-LinUCB (Guo--Xu no-intercept) recursion: two arms; contexts \(X_t\) drawn independently and uniformly from \(\{-4,1\}\); rewards \(Y_t(1)=1/2+\sigma_1R_{t,1}\) and \(Y_t(2)=1/12+\sigma_2R_{t,2}\) with independent centered Rademacher innovations \(R_{t,a}\) and arbitrary fixed \(\sigma_1,\sigma_2>0\); unit-precision ridge states \(\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}+\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}X_t^2\) and \(b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}+\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}X_tY_t\), slopes \(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}/\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), inverse Gram \(q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=1/\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), and the augmented time-homogeneous Markov state \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t\) on the compact set \(\mathsf E_{\mathrm{GX}}=[-M_{\mathrm{GX}},M_{\mathrm{GX}}]^2\times[0,1]^2\); at each occasion the index \(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}X_t+|X_t|\sqrt{q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}}\) is maximized with ties broken to arm \(1\) and the maximizer is assigned with probability \(0.99\); the chain is started at \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_0=\iota_{\mathrm{GX}}(\eta_0)\) for \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}=[-1,1]^2\), inducing the law \(P_{\eta_0}\). The ambient limit object is the normalized state \(\Psi_t=(D_{t,1}/t,D_{t,2}/t,N_{t,1}/t,N_{t,2}/t)\) together with the closed convexified differential inclusion \(\dot\psi\in F(\psi)\) it perturbs. — The chain law \(P_{\eta_0}\) is built by Ionescu--Tulcea composition of the one-step kernel (`Mathlib.Probability.Kernel.IonescuTulcea.Traj`, file confirmed at `.lake/packages/mathlib/Mathlib/Probability/Kernel/IonescuTulcea/Traj.lean`). standard.citation: Yongyi Guo and Ziping Xu. Statistical Inference for Misspecified Contextual Bandits. arXiv:2606.22639v1, 21 June 2026.

nl.statement: Conditional on \(X_t\) and \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\), the action \(A_t\) is drawn from the logged distribution \(\pi_t(\cdot\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})\) independently of \((Y_t(a))_{a\in\mathcal A}\).

review.note: The pre-treatment σ-field is exactly σ(F_{t-1},X_t), singleton conditional probabilities equal the logged finite-arm policy, and measurable-rectangle factorization gives the stated conditional independence from the complete potential-outcome vector.

standard.citation: Tianchen Qian and coauthors. The Micro-Randomized Trial for Developing Digital Interventions. Psychological Methods 27, 2022.

nl.statement: For every \(a\in\mathcal A\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(\eta\in\mathsf H\), the policy satisfies \(\Pi(a\mid x,\eta)\ge\varepsilon\).

review.note: The universal policy lower bound is exactly the paper condition; 0<ε<1/K merely realizes the frozen symbol domain ε∈(0,1/K).

standard.name: Policy-wide clipped adaptive overlap
standard.citation: Yongyi Guo and Ziping Xu. Statistical Inference for Misspecified Contextual Bandits. arXiv:2606.22639v1, 21 June 2026.

nl.statement: The common envelope satisfies \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal A,\theta\in\Theta}\|g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)\|_2\le B\) almost surely.

review.note: For every decision time, the almost-sure universal bound over all arms and θ∈Θ is equivalent to the stated pointwise supremum envelope; positivity of B realizes its frozen symbol domain.

standard.name: Bounded martingale increments
standard.citation: Jean-Christophe Mourrat. On the Rate of Convergence in the Martingale Central Limit Theorem. Bernoulli 19, 2013.

nl.statement: The map \(\theta\mapsto g(a,x,y;\theta)\) is continuously differentiable on a common open neighborhood of \(\operatorname{conv}(\Theta)\), with \(\|\partial_\theta g(a,x,y;\theta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le D_1\) there, and is twice continuously differentiable on the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), with \(\|\partial_\theta^2 g(a,x,y;\theta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le D_2\) throughout that ball.

review.note: The shared open set contains conv(Θ), carries C¹ regularity and the D₁ operator-norm bound, while the closed ρ-ball carries C² regularity and the D₂ second-derivative operator-norm bound; positivity realizes the frozen parameter domains.

standard.citation: Yongyi Guo and Ziping Xu. Statistical Inference for Misspecified Contextual Bandits. arXiv:2606.22639v1, 21 June 2026.

review.note: The pointwise lower bound over every θ ∈ Θ with ‖θ−θ*‖ ≥ u is equivalent to the stated infimum bound, and κ(u)>0 is explicitly required by the frozen constant declaration.

nl.statement: The common policy modulus satisfies \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal A,x\in\mathcal X}|\Pi(a\mid x,\eta)-\Pi(a\mid x,\eta')|\le L_\Pi\|\eta-\eta'\|_2\) for all \(\eta,\eta'\in\mathsf H\).

review.note: The supremum bound is equivalent to the displayed pointwise bound over all arms and contexts; the added 0≤LΠ follows by taking η'=η on the nonempty state space.

nl.statement: There exists a \(\sigma(\bigcup_{t\ge1}\mathcal F_t)\)-measurable \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\)-valued random variable \(J\) such that \(\eta_\infty=\bar\eta_J\) almost surely.

review.note: The Fin m label is a harmless reindexing of {1,…,m}, the filtration supremum is the σ-algebra generated by the increasing filtration union, and the equality is almost sure under E.law.

The Lean event is exactly the Cesàro-distance event in the note, with `dist` representing the state-space ℓ₂ distance and `Finset.Icc 1 T` representing t=1,…,T; the T=0 clause is automatic on the core-declared nonnegative r_T and δ_T domain.

nl.statement: The common deterministic error envelope satisfies \(e_T=T^{-1/2}+r_T+\delta_T\to0\).

review.note: The Tendsto conjunct is exactly e_T=T⁻¹ᐟ²+r_T+δ_T→0, while the two nonnegativity conjuncts merely realize the core-declared domains of r_T and δ_T.

nl.statement: The terminal covariance satisfies \(\Omega_\infty\succeq\omega_-I_d\) almost surely.

review.note: `psdLE (omegaMin • identMat d) (omegaInf ω)` unfolds to the quadratic-form Loewner inequality Ω∞(ω) ⪰ ω_-I_d almost surely, and omegaMin>0 is the core-declared domain of ω_-.
Fin m indexes exactly the m attractors and Euclidean dist gives the stated pairwise L2 bound; 0 < sEta merely makes explicit the core-declared domain s_eta in (0,infinity).

The final conjunct is exactly P(J=j)≥p_- for every j, while 0<pmin≤1/m is the core-declared domain of p_- and is also forced by these bounds for a probability law over the measurable Fin m-valued label.

After unfolding the law, filtration, projected-score aliases, and UniformInProbability-style quantifiers, Lean states the same uniform suffix predictable-QV convergence; omega > 0 and the almost-sure floor also give the paper's almost-sure positivity of Lambda.

nl.statement: For fixed \(m\), \(\bar\eta_1,\ldots,\bar\eta_m\), \(s_\eta\), \(p_-\), \(\varepsilon,B,D_1,D_2,h_-,L_\Pi,\omega_-,\kappa,s_\Theta,\rho\), and common sequences \((r_T,\delta_T)_{T\ge1}\), define \(\mathfrak P_T\) to be the set of laws \(P\) that, at horizon \(T\), satisfy every condition in \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}full\text{-}data},\ldots,\mathrm{ass:basin\text{-}nondegeneracy}\) with these common objects, envelopes, and moduli. The fixed states obey \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}attractor\text{-}separation}\), the terminal label and selected state obey \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}tail\text{-}selection}\), every label obeys \(\mathrm{ass:basin\text{-}mass\text{-}floor}\), and the path approximation is supplied solely by \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}attraction\text{-}modulus}\). Thus \(\eta_\infty=\bar\eta_J\), every one of the \(m\) separated basins has mass at least \(p_-\), and the policy path is approximated by its selected attractor only through the uniform Cesaro inequality. Pointwise convergence of \(\eta_t\) is not imposed.

review.note: The structure bundles exactly the stated finite-attractor assumptions; attractor/state membership and the radius inequalities are intrinsic symbol-domain constraints, and the only path restriction is the stated Cesaro attraction modulus.

nl.statement: First choose a measurable preliminary estimator \(\widetilde\theta_T\in\Theta\) satisfying \(\|G_T(\widetilde\theta_T)\|_2\le\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}\|G_T(\theta)\|_2+T^{-1/2}(r_T+\delta_T)\), using a fixed measurable tie-breaking rule. Define the compact correspondence \(\mathcal Z_T=\{\theta\in\Theta:G_T(\theta)=0,\ \|\theta-\widetilde\theta_T\|_2\le\rho/2\}\) and \(E_T=\{\mathcal Z_T\ne\varnothing\}\). Continuity of \(G_T\) on compact \(\Theta\) makes \(\mathcal Z_T\) compact, and its standard joint measurability permits a fixed measurable lexicographic compact-set selector. On \(E_T\), let \(\widehat\theta_T\) be that selected member of \(\mathcal Z_T\); on \(E_T^c\), set \(\widehat\theta_T=\widetilde\theta_T\).

nl.statement: For every \(T\ge2\), let \(P^{\dagger}\) be the law with \(K=3\), \(d=2\), \(\Theta=[-1,1]^2\), \(\theta^*=0\), a singleton \(\mathcal X\), and constant \(X_t\). Independently across \(t\) and between arms, let \(Y_t(1)\) be equiprobable on \(\{-\sqrt{2/5},\sqrt{2/5}\}\), let \(Y_t(2)\) be equiprobable on \(\{-\sqrt{1/2},\sqrt{1/2}\}\), and set \(Y_t(3)=0\). Set \(g(1,x,y;\theta)=(y-\theta_1,0)^\top\), \(g(2,x,y;\theta)=(0,y-\theta_2)^\top\), and \(g(3,x,y;\theta)=0\). Take \(m=2\), \(q=1\), \(\mathsf H=[0,1]\), \(\bar\eta_1=0\), \(\bar\eta_2=1\), and linearly interpolate the context-free policy between \(\Pi(\cdot\mid x,0)=(2/5,1/4,7/20)\) and \(\Pi(\cdot\mid x,1)=(2/5,1/6,13/30)\). Start at \(\eta_0=1/2\), set \(J=1\) if and only if \(A_1=1\), set \(J=2\) otherwise, define \(\eta_\infty=\bar\eta_J=J-1\), and put \(\eta_t=\eta_\infty\) for every \(t\ge1\).

nl.statement:
For \(\eta\in\mathsf H\), define
\[
 \Gamma_P(\eta)=E_P\!\left[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}
 \frac{g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta^*)g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta^*)^\top}
 {\Pi(a\mid X_t,\eta)}\right].
\]
For every \(j\in\mathcal J=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), set
\[
 p_j=P(J=j),\qquad
 \Omega_j=\Gamma_P(\bar\eta_j),\qquad
 V_j=H^{-1}\Omega_jH^{-\top}.
\]
Define
\[
 \Omega_J=\sum_{j=1}^m\mathbf1\{J=j\}\Omega_j,\qquad
 V_J=\sum_{j=1}^m\mathbf1\{J=j\}V_j,
\]
and set
\[
 \Omega_\infty=\Gamma_P(\eta_\infty),\qquad
 V_\infty=H^{-1}\Omega_\infty H^{-\top}.
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}tail\text{-}selection}\), substitution of \(\eta_\infty=\bar\eta_J\) gives \(\Omega_\infty=\Omega_J\) and \(V_\infty=V_J\) almost surely.

nl.statement:
Set
\[
 \widehat\Omega_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\widehat\xi_t\widehat\xi_t^\top,
 \qquad
 \mathcal H_T=\{\sigma_{\min}(\widehat H_T)\ge h_-/2\}.
\]
Define the total nonnegative scalar
\[
 \widehat q_T(c)=
 \begin{cases}
 c^\top\widehat H_T^{-1}\widehat\Omega_T\widehat H_T^{-\top}c,
   &\text{on }\mathcal H_T,\\
 0,&\text{on }\mathcal H_T^c,
 \end{cases}
\]
where the inverse is evaluated only on \(\mathcal H_T\), and set
\[
 \mathcal E_T(c)=\mathcal H_T\cap\{\widehat q_T(c)\ge\omega_{c,T}/2\}.
\]
Define the total early-scale event-truncated sandwich by
\[
 \widehat V_T(c)=
 \begin{cases}
 \widehat H_T^{-1}\widehat\Omega_T\widehat H_T^{-\top},
   &\text{on }\mathcal E_T(c),\\
 I_d,&\text{on }\mathcal E_T(c)^c.
 \end{cases}
\]
Thus every inverse is evaluated only on \(\mathcal H_T\), and \(c^\top\widehat V_T(c)c>0\) for every realization because \(c\ne0\).

nl.statement:
For the prespecified nonzero \(c\), use the early-scale event-truncated sandwich \(\widehat V_T(c)\) and define the everywhere finite statistic
\[
 T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)=
 \frac{\sqrt T\,c^\top(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)}
 {\sqrt{c^\top\widehat V_T(c)c}}.
\]
The denominator is positive on every realization by the construction of \(\widehat V_T(c)\).

Unfolding qform and probit yields exactly the closed interval centered at cᵀθ̂_T with half-width z_{1-α/2}√(cᵀΣc/T), on the stated positive-T, positive-definite-Σ, nonzero-c, and α∈(0,1) domain.

nl.statement: Fix \(K=2\), draw \(X_t\) independently and uniformly from \(\{-4,1\}\), and set \(Y_t(1)=1/2+\sigma_1R_{t,1}\) and \(Y_t(2)=1/12+\sigma_2R_{t,2}\), where the \(R_{t,a}\) are independent centered Rademacher innovations and \(\sigma_1,\sigma_2>0\) are arbitrary fixed constants declared as part of this bounded analogue; no numerical innovation variances are attributed to Guo and Xu. Keep their no-intercept working model, ridge constant \(\lambda=1\), unit-precision ridge initialization, and updates \(\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}+\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}X_t^2\), \(b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}+\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}X_tY_t\), and \(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}/\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\). For \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\), initialize \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_0=\iota_{\mathrm{GX}}(\eta_0)=(\eta_{0,1},\eta_{0,2},1,1)^\top\), equivalently \(\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{0,a}=1\) and \(b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{0,a}=\eta_{0,a}\); the published initialization is the included case \(\eta_0=(0,0)^\top\). At occasion \(t\), break every exact index tie in favor of arm \(1\), maximize \(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}X_t+|X_t|\sqrt{q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}}\), and then assign the maximizing arm with probability \(0.99\) and the other arm with probability \(0.01\). The process of interest is the slope projection \((\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top\) of \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t\), not a slope-only Markov chain.

review.note: Unfolding the initial state, reward, index, tie-broken greedy arm, clipped assignment, step, context, and canonical product noise law gives the bounded two-arm recursion, initialization, 0.99/0.01 allocation, independent uniform contexts and Rademacher innovations, with slopes and inverse Grams recoverable from the full state.

nl.statement: Write \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t=(\beta_1,\beta_2,q_1,q_2)^\top\) for a current augmented state. Its induced armwise update is \(q_a^+=q_a/(1+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aX^2)\) and \(\beta_a^+=(\beta_a+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aXY(a))/(1+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aX^2)\). The next clipped-UCB action uses \(\beta_aX+|X|\sqrt{q_a}\), so \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t\), rather than its two-dimensional slope projection, is the time-homogeneous Markov state. For stochastic-approximation analysis, put \(D_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), \(N_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), and, for \(t\ge1\), \(\Psi_t=(D_{t,1}/t,D_{t,2}/t,N_{t,1}/t,N_{t,2}/t)\). Analyze the exact \(1/(t+1)\) recursion for \(\Psi_t\) on an eventually compact region with both normalized Gram coordinates bounded away from zero. At the equal-slope surface, retain every limiting conditional-mean mode generated by the square-root UCB bonus: although the bonus is \(O(t^{-1/2})\), it can make the same arm greedy at both contexts inside an \(O(t^{-1/2})\) switching layer. Thus a closed convexified limiting graph must include these same-arm modes as well as the two opposite-context modes. Any differential-inclusion reduction must verify the closed-graph, compact-convex-value, boundedness, vanishing-perturbation, and martingale-tail conditions for this normalized recursion. Compact-uniform sequences \(r_T(K_0),\delta_T(K_0)\to0\) require a separate quantitative hitting or escape estimate and may not be inferred from pointwise convergence by a finite-cover argument.

review.note: Replace the vacuous martingale-tail and quantitative-hitting/escape sequence fields with bounds tied to the recursion and K0, include the quantitative alternative in the reduction predicate, and state closed-graph continuity relative to an actual compact positive-Gram region rather than ambient closedness of the graph over the open positive-Gram domain.

nl.statement:
For the prespecified nonzero \(c\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), use the early-scale event-truncated sandwich and define the total Wald interval
\[
 I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)=
 \left[\widehat\tau_T-z_{1-\alpha/2}
 \sqrt{c^\top\widehat V_T(c)c/T},\ 
 \widehat\tau_T+z_{1-\alpha/2}
 \sqrt{c^\top\widehat V_T(c)c/T}\right].
\]

nl.statement:
Fix a prespecified \(c\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}\), the common objects \(\varepsilon,B,D_1,D_2,h_-,\kappa,s_\Theta,\rho,\Theta\), deterministic tolerance sequences \((r_T,\delta_T)_{T\ge1}\), deterministic integers \(0\le k_T<T\), and deterministic numbers \(\omega_{c,T}>0\) satisfying
\[
 T\omega_{c,T}\longrightarrow\infty,
 \qquad
 \frac{k_T}{T\omega_{c,T}}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Let \((\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c))_{T\ge1}\) be any chosen sequence of law classes such that every \(P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)\) satisfies
\[
 \mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}full\text{-}data},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:sequential\text{-}randomization},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}overlap},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}score},
\]
\[
 \mathrm{ass:smooth\text{-}z\text{-}map},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}root\text{-}separation},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:root\text{-}interior},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:jacobian\text{-}nonsingular},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:vanishing\text{-}modulus}.
\]
For each member law there must exist a positive random scale \(\Lambda_T\), measurable with respect to \(\mathcal F_{k_T}\), such that \(\Lambda_T\ge\omega_{c,T}\) almost surely and the chosen class sequence satisfies \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}projected\text{-}predictable\text{-}qv\text{-}growth}\). No information-growth condition is imposed in a direction orthogonal to \(H^{-\top}c\), and neither finite attractors nor convergence of the full matrix \(T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T\) is required.

review.note: Lean is strictly narrower: radius_range imposes rho < sTheta and D2*rho/epsilon < hmin/4, neither stated in the paper class definition nor entailed by its enumerated assumptions; remove this field from the class.

nl.statement:
For each row \(n\), let \(\mathcal T_n=\{t_{n,1}<\cdots<t_{n,N_n}\}\) be a deterministic scored set, fixed before data collection, and put \(N_n=n_{\mathrm{eff}}=|\mathcal T_n|\).  The class \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{Saco,es}}=(\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{Saco,es}})_{n\ge1}\) consists of triangular arrays of binary-treatment laws with the following properties, imposed row by row and uniformly over the displayed class.

First, the source conditions retained from Saco are written out explicitly.  For \(a\in\{0,1\}\), \(Y_{n,t}(a)\) is the potential outcome depending only on the current treatment, and \(Y_{n,t}=A_{n,t}Y_{n,t}(1)+(1-A_{n,t})Y_{n,t}(0)\) almost surely.  The triples \((X_{n,t},Y_{n,t}(0),Y_{n,t}(1))\) are independent and identically distributed over \(t\) within a row and are unaffected by the adaptive policy.  There is a pre-treatment sigma-field \(\mathcal B_{n,t}\), containing the past and \(X_{n,t}\), such that the logged propensity \(\pi_{n,t}\) is \(\mathcal B_{n,t}\)-measurable and
\[
0<\pi_{n,t}<1,\qquad
\mathbb P_n(A_{n,t}=1\mid\mathcal B_{n,t})=\pi_{n,t}\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
Conditional on \(\mathcal B_{n,t}\), \(A_{n,t}\) is independent of \((Y_{n,t}(0),Y_{n,t}(1))\).  There is one constant \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\) such that
\[
\epsilon\le\pi_{n,t}\le1-\epsilon
\quad\text{almost surely for every }t\in\mathcal T_n.
\]
For each \(a\), the fitted regression \(\widehat m_{n,t-1,a}\), as a random function, is measurable with respect to the history \(\mathcal F_{n,t-1}\).  There are finite constants \(C_Y,C_M\), common to the class, such that
\[
\sup_{n,\mathbb P_n,t,a}E_{\mathbb P_n}|Y_{n,t}(a)|^4\le C_Y,\qquad
\sup_{n,\mathbb P_n,t\in\mathcal T_n,a}
E_{\mathbb P_n}|\widehat m_{n,t-1,a}(X_{n,t})|^4\le C_M.
\]
Thus these are uniform versions of source Assumptions \(3.5,3.6,3.2,3.7,3.8,4.5,4.8,3.9,\) and \(3.10\), in the order specified by the directive.

Define the causal target, AIPW pseudo-outcome, centered score, estimator, and its sample variance by
\[
\theta_{0,n}=E_{\mathbb P_n}\{Y_{n,t}(1)-Y_{n,t}(0)\},
\]
\[
\widehat\phi_{n,t}=\frac{A_{n,t}}{\pi_{n,t}}
\{Y_{n,t}-\widehat m_{n,t-1,1}(X_{n,t})\}
-\frac{1-A_{n,t}}{1-\pi_{n,t}}
\{Y_{n,t}-\widehat m_{n,t-1,0}(X_{n,t})\}
+\widehat m_{n,t-1,1}(X_{n,t})-\widehat m_{n,t-1,0}(X_{n,t}),
\]
\[
X_{n,s}=\widehat\phi_{n,t_{n,s}}-\theta_{0,n},\qquad
S_n=\sum_{s=1}^{N_n}X_{n,s},\qquad
Q_n=\sum_{s=1}^{N_n}X_{n,s}^2,
\]
\[
\widehat\theta_n=N_n^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^{N_n}\widehat\phi_{n,t_{n,s}},\qquad
\widehat V_n=(N_n-1)^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^{N_n}
\{\widehat\phi_{n,t_{n,s}}-\widehat\theta_n\}^2
\quad(N_n\ge2).
\]
To order the deterministic scored set without discarding interstitial history, define
\[
\mathcal G_{n,0}=\mathcal F_{n,t_{n,1}-1},\qquad
\mathcal G_{n,s}=\mathcal F_{n,t_{n,s+1}-1}\ (1\le s<N_n),\qquad
\mathcal G_{n,N_n}=\mathcal F_{n,t_{n,N_n}}.
\]
Then \(X_{n,s}\) is \(\mathcal G_{n,s}\)-measurable and \(\mathcal G_{n,s-1}=\mathcal F_{n,t_{n,s}-1}\).  Put
\[
V_n^2=\sum_{s=1}^{N_n}E_{\mathbb P_n}[X_{n,s}^2\mid\mathcal G_{n,s-1}].
\]
The source variance-growth Assumption \(5.11\) is retained: \(N_n\to\infty\), and for one \(v_->0\),
\[
\sup_{\mathbb P_n\in\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{Saco,es}}}
\mathbb P_n(V_n^2<v_-N_n)\longrightarrow0.
\]

Finally, intersect those source conditions with early quadratic-variation stabilization.  There are deterministic integers \(0\le k_n<N_n\), a constant \(\lambda_->0\), and, for every member law, a positive \(\mathcal G_{n,k_n}\)-measurable random variable \(\Lambda_n\) such that
\[
\frac{k_n}{N_n}\longrightarrow0,\qquad \Lambda_n\ge\lambda_-\quad\text{almost surely},
\]
and, writing
\[
A_{n,+}^2=\sum_{s=k_n+1}^{N_n}
E_{\mathbb P_n}[X_{n,s}^2\mid\mathcal G_{n,s-1}],
\]
one has, for every \(\zeta>0\),
\[
\sup_{\mathbb P_n\in\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{Saco,es}}}
\mathbb P_n\left(\left|\frac{A_{n,+}^2}{N_n\Lambda_n}-1\right|>\zeta\right)\longrightarrow0.
\]
Consequently \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{Saco,es}}\) is exactly Saco's enumerated AIPW/DML class, with the overlap and fourth-moment constants made uniform across the triangular array, intersected with this early-measurable suffix-QV condition.  No almost-sure bound on \(X_{n,s}\) is imposed.

review.note: After unfolding SacoSourceConditions, SacoArrayWorld, and UniformInProbability, the rowwise source conditions, common deterministic scored sets, uniform variance growth, early measurable positive scales, negligible cutoff, and uniform suffix-QV stabilization match the paper; the Lambda parameter conservatively chooses the per-member witnesses.

nl.statement:
The common derivative and bounded-IPW envelopes imply
\[
 \|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KD_1,
 \qquad
 \omega_-I_d\preceq\Omega_j\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d
 \quad\text{for every }j\in\mathcal J=\{1,\ldots,m\}.
\]
The finite-tail-selection relation gives \(\Omega_\infty=\Omega_J\) and \(V_\infty=V_J\) almost surely. There is a finite constant \(C\), independent of \(T\) and \(P\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}E_P\!\left[
 \left\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_J\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\right]
 \le C(r_T+\delta_T).
\]
The preliminary estimator is uniformly consistent, \(G_T(\theta^*)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\), and \(\partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})\) uniformly. Together with \(D_2\rho/\varepsilon<h_-/4\), these bounds imply that, with probability tending uniformly to one, there is a unique empirical root in the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), it is \(O_P(T^{-1/2})\) from \(\theta^*\), and it is the unique member of \(\mathcal Z_T\). Hence \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(E_T^c)\to0\), and
\[
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T=O_P(e_T)
\]
uniformly.

For every basin \(j\in\mathcal J\), the basin-conditional Gaussian approximation is uniform:
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\!\left\{c^\top\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)\le z\mid J=j\right\}
 -\Phi\!\left(\frac{z}{\sqrt{c^\top V_jc}}\right)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
More strongly, the corresponding joint \(\sigma(J)\)-stable Gaussian kernel is expressed by
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \sup_{\psi:\{1,\ldots,m\}\to[-1,1]}
 \left|E_P\!\left[\psi(J)\mathbf1\!\left\{
 c^\top\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)\le z\right\}\right]
 -\sum_{j=1}^mp_j\psi(j)\Phi\!\left(\frac{z}{\sqrt{c^\top V_jc}}\right)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \frac{\omega_-}{(KD_1)^2}I_d\preceq V_j
 \preceq\frac{KB^2}{\varepsilon h_-^2}I_d
 \quad\text{for every }j\in\mathcal J.
\]
Thus, for every sequence \(P_T\in\mathfrak P_T\), the laws of \(V_J\) have a weakly convergent subsequence with a limiting law \(\mu\) supported on the displayed compact covariance set. Along that subsequence, every fixed nonzero contrast has the centered Gaussian scale-mixture limit \(\sqrt{c^\top Vc}\,Z_1\), where \(V\sim\mu\), \(Z_1\sim N(0,1)\), and \(V\) and \(Z_1\) are independent. This limit is Gaussian if and only if \(c^\top Vc\) is \(\mu\)-almost surely constant. No pointwise convergence of \(\eta_t\) is used.

review.note: Lean⇒paper fails for the covariance-law conclusion: `[MeasurableSpace (Mat d)]` is unconstrained, so the weak-convergence and mixture integrals need not use the Euclidean Borel structure, while the stated `psdLE` support admits nonsymmetric skew perturbations and is not the paper's compact covariance set; require `[BorelSpace (Mat d)]` and explicitly use `covarianceInterval` or add transpose symmetry.

nl.statement:
Fix a prespecified \(c\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}\). For the early-stabilized projected class \(\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)\), the exact-root event is uniformly asymptotically certain and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}P(E_T^c)\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T
 =O_P(T^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly. Moreover,
\[
 T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat\Omega_T-T^{-1}[S]_T=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat H_T-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly over that class. Although no information growth is required outside the direction \(H^{-\top}c\), the early-scale condition with \(T\omega_{c,T}\to\infty\) makes the contrast-specific truncation inactive:
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}P\{\mathcal E_T(c)^c\}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\{T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)\le z\}-\Phi(z)\right|
 \longrightarrow0,
\]
and, for every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}
 \left|P\{\tau\in I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)\}-(1-\alpha)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Every finite-tail-attractor class \(\mathfrak P_T\) satisfies this early-stabilized condition for each fixed nonzero \(c\). At every horizon set
\[
 k_T=\min\!\left\{T-1,\left\lceil T\max\{T^{-1/2},\sqrt{r_T}\}\right\rceil\right\}.
\]
For \(k_T\ge1\), let \(J_T\) be the nearest attractor to \(k_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{k_T}\eta_{t-1}\), with fixed tie-breaking, and set \(J_T=1\) when \(k_T=0\). With \(a=H^{-\top}c\), take
\[
 \Lambda_T=a^\top\Omega_{J_T}a,\qquad
 \omega_{c,T}=\frac{\omega_-\|c\|_2^2}{(KD_1)^2}.
\]
Then \(J_T\) and \(\Lambda_T\) are \(\mathcal F_{k_T}\)-measurable, all early-scale conditions hold uniformly, and the same pivot and coverage conclusions follow.

review.note: Neither direction is established for the finite-attractor clause: Lean conditions it on an unrelated projected-class witness hClass, omits the nearest-attractor and kFinite T = 0 default specifications for the same Jearly used in LambdaFinite, and—unlike the projected branch—does not link CF's r/failure or EF's Jacobian derivative to the finite-class data; restate this as an independent implication for every hFinite with an explicit c ≠ 0 premise, the required contract/Jacobian coherence, and the canonical nearest/default Jearly clauses.

nl.statement:
Let \(T_\ell\to\infty\) and \(P_\ell\in\mathfrak P_{T_\ell}\) be a sequence along which the law of \(V_\infty\) under \(P_\ell\) converges weakly to a probability law \(\mu\) on the compact covariance set in Theorem 1. Let \(V\sim\mu\). Fix nonzero \(c\) and deterministic positive-definite \(\Sigma\). Then
\[
 \lim_{\ell\to\infty}P_\ell\{\tau\in C_{T_\ell}^{\Sigma}(c,\alpha)\}=1-\alpha
 \quad\text{for every }\alpha\in(0,1)
\]
if and only if
\[
 c^\top Vc=c^\top\Sigma c\qquad\mu\text{-almost surely}.
\]
The necessity identifies the projected variance law of a general centered Gaussian scale mixture from coverage at every nominal level; it makes no claim from validity at only one level.

review.note: Paper ⇒ Lean fails: P_l ∈ 𝔓_{T_l} requires the Cesàro attraction bound only at horizon T_l, but unfolding S.member and UniformAttractionModulus requires each P_l to satisfy it at every natural horizon n; parameterize the predicate by the member horizon and instantiate it at S.T l.

nl.statement:
Along any sequence for which the law of \(V_\infty\) converges weakly to \(\mu\), as in Theorem 3, one deterministic positive-definite matrix \(\Sigma\) gives asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and every nonzero contrast \(c\in\mathbb R^d\) if and only if
\[
 V=\Sigma\qquad\mu\text{-almost surely},
\]
where \(V\sim\mu\). Equivalently, the limiting covariance law is the point mass at \(\Sigma\). For a fixed law and horizon-asymptotic sequence, this specializes to \(V_\infty=\Sigma\) almost surely whenever the law of \(V_\infty\) itself is constant across horizons. The implication from all projected equalities to matrix equality uses only finitely many coordinate and pairwise-sum contrasts.

\[
D\le C_{p,\gamma}\left\{\frac{n\log n}{s^3}+\left(\|V^2-1\|_p^p+s^{-2p}\right)^{1/(2p+1)}\right\}.
\]

Let \(\lambda_T\) be \(\mathcal G_{T,k_T}\)-measurable and satisfy \(0<v_-\le\lambda_T\le v_+<\infty\) almost surely. If
\[
 \Delta_T:=E_P\left|T^{-1}\sum_{t=k_T+1}^T
 E_P[X_{T,t}^2\mid\mathcal G_{T,t-1}]-\lambda_T\right|\longrightarrow0,

 -E_P\Phi\left(\frac{z}{\sqrt{\lambda_T}}\right)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
The conclusion is uniform over any collection of arrays having common \(L,v_-,v_+\) and a common upper bound on \(\Delta_T\) that tends to zero.

nl.statement:
Consider the bounded-noise Guo--Xu recursion with arbitrary fixed \(\sigma_1,\sigma_2>0\) and deterministic tie arm \(1\). Put \(p=99/100\), \(q=1/100\), and, for \((u,v)\in[q,p]^2\), define
\[
 h(u,v)=\left(\frac{u+16v}{2},\frac{17-u-16v}{2},
                 \frac{u-4v}{4},\frac{-3-u+4v}{24}\right).
\]
For \(t\ge1\), put \(D_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), \(N_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), and \(\Psi_t=(D_{t,1}/t,D_{t,2}/t,N_{t,1}/t,N_{t,2}/t)\). Then \(q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=O(t^{-1})\) almost surely, \(\Psi_t\) obeys an exact stochastic-approximation recursion with step \(1/(t+1)\), and its affine interpolation is a bounded perturbed solution, hence an asymptotic pseudotrajectory, of the closed convexified inclusion \(\dot\psi\in F(\psi)\) below. Writing \(\Delta(\psi)=n_1/d_1-n_2/d_2\), \(h_+=h(p,q)\), \(h_-=h(q,p)\), \(h_1=h(p,p)\), and \(h_2=h(q,q)\), its graph on \(d_1,d_2>0\) is
\[
 F(\psi)=
 \begin{cases}
  \{h_+-\psi\},&\Delta(\psi)>0,\\
  \{h_--\psi\},&\Delta(\psi)<0,\\
  \operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_1\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1<d_2,\\
  \operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_2\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1>d_2,\\
  \operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_1,h_2\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1=d_2.
 \end{cases}
\]
Every almost-sure normalized-state limit set is internally chain transitive for \(F\) and is contained in the computable parallelogram \(\mathcal C=\{h(u,v):(u,v)\in[q,p]^2\}\); the projected slope limit set is its continuous image under \((d_1,d_2,n_1,n_2)\mapsto(n_1/d_1,n_2/d_2)\).

The smaller inclusion having only \(h_+-\psi\), \(h_--\psi\), and \(\operatorname{co}\{h_+-\psi,h_--\psi\}\) on the switching surface is not a valid unconditional reduction of this recursion. If it were the limiting inclusion, its only internally chain-transitive sets would be the three singletons \(\{h_-\}\), \(\{h(u_0,1-u_0)\}\), and \(\{h_+\}\), where
\[
 u_0=\frac{47+\sqrt{4609}}{150},\qquad
 \frac{N_1}{D_1}=\frac{N_2}{D_2}
 =b_0:=\frac{\sqrt{4609}-91}{1224}
 \quad\text{at }h(u_0,1-u_0).
\]
The correct graph instead has an uncountable family of additional internally chain-transitive singleton equilibria. Explicitly, for
\[
 u\in[u_0,p],\qquad
 v(u)=\frac{3u+18-\sqrt{25u^2-228u+324}}{32},
\]
one has \(h(u,v(u))\in\mathcal C\), equal slope coordinates, first normalized Gram coordinate smaller than the second, and \(0\in F(h(u,v(u)))\). In particular,
\[
 v_*:=v(p)=\frac{2097}{3200}-\frac{3\sqrt{5457}}{640}
\]
gives an equilibrium \(h(p,v_*)\) distinct from \(h_-\), \(h(u_0,1-u_0)\), and \(h_+\). This continuum is an explicit internally-chain-transitive obstruction to a three-candidate conclusion from the standard differential-inclusion route.

For the actual recursion, on \(\mathcal L_+=\{\liminf_t(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1}-\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})>0\}\) and \(\mathcal L_-=\{\limsup_t(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1}-\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})<0\}\), respectively,
\[
 (\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top
 \longrightarrow
 \left(\frac{19}{46},-\frac{79}{3804}\right)^\top
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \left(-\frac{79}{634},\frac{19}{276}\right)^\top.
\]
Both events have probability bounded away from zero uniformly over \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\), and the corresponding pathwise Cesaro errors converge to zero. If both slopes have a common-coordinate subsequential limit and \((u,v)\) is a simultaneous subsequential limit of the empirical conditional arm-\(1\) rates, then necessarily
\[
 u^2+12uv-21u-64v^2+72v=0.
\]
The relation \(v=1-u\), and hence the candidate \((u_0,b_0)\), is justified only if same-arm switching-layer occupation is separately excluded; the exact recursion does not provide that exclusion. Consequently, this argument proves neither finite almost-sure tail selection nor zero probability of switching-surface convergence. It also proves no compact-initial-set uniform attraction moduli \(r_T(K_0),\delta_T(K_0)\). These are dynamics-only conclusions: they assert neither membership in \(\mathfrak P_T\) nor applicability of any inference theorem.

nl.statement:
There is a bounded two-arm, one-dimensional adaptive IPW-Z experiment targeting the causal arm-mean contrast \(\theta^*=E[Y_t(1)]-E[Y_t(2)]\), with uniform overlap and nonsingular Jacobian, for which \(T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T\ge4\) almost surely but the realized-QV score pivot, and hence its feasible IPW-Z counterpart, has a nonstandard noncentered limit. Specifically, at horizons \(T=2n\), the limit is
\[
 L=\mathbf1\{Z>0\}\frac{2Z+4W/\sqrt3}{\sqrt{28/3}}
 +\mathbf1\{Z\le0\}\frac{2Z+2W}{\sqrt8},
\]
where \(Z,W\) are independent \(N(0,1)\) variables, and
\[
 E[L]=\frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi}}
 \left(\sqrt{\frac3{28}}-\frac1{\sqrt8}\right)\ne0.
\]
Thus a predictable-QV lower floor and realized-to-predictable QV consistency do not suffice for a Gaussian self-normalized pivot when an early score selects the later variance regime.

review.note: Neither implication follows: the paper fixes the feasible pivot's truncation scale at omega=4, giving threshold qhat_T(1)>=2, while Lean passes omega=2 and therefore uses threshold 1; instantiate realizedQVPivot with omega=4.

nl.statement:
Let \((X_{n,t},\mathcal G_{n,t})_{t=1}^{N_n}\) be a scalar martingale-difference triangular array, where \(N_n\) and \(h_n\) are deterministic integers satisfying \(0\le h_n<N_n\), and suppose \(|X_{n,t}|\le L<\infty\) almost surely. Let \(\lambda_n\) be a positive \(\mathcal G_{n,h_n}\)-measurable random variable, and let \(\nu_n>0\) be deterministic with \(\lambda_n\ge\nu_n\) almost surely. Define
\[
 S_n=\sum_{t=1}^{N_n}X_{n,t},\qquad
 Q_n=\sum_{t=1}^{N_n}X_{n,t}^2,\qquad
 A_{n,+}^2=\sum_{t=h_n+1}^{N_n}E[X_{n,t}^2\mid\mathcal G_{n,t-1}].
\]
If
\[
 N_n\nu_n\longrightarrow\infty,\qquad
 \frac{h_n}{N_n\nu_n}\longrightarrow0,\qquad
 \frac{A_{n,+}^2}{N_n\lambda_n}\longrightarrow1
 \quad\text{in probability},
\]
then
\[
 \frac{Q_n}{N_n\lambda_n}\longrightarrow1
 \quad\text{in probability},\qquad
 P(Q_n>0)\longrightarrow1,\qquad
 \frac{S_n}{\sqrt{Q_n}}\Rightarrow N(0,1).
\]
All conclusions are uniform over a collection of arrays if \(L\) is common and each displayed convergence premise is uniform over that collection.

review.note: Unfolding the array and uniform-convergence definitions gives exactly the bounded martingale-array premises and the three uniform conclusions, with the self-normalized ratio set to zero when Q_n = 0.

nl.statement: Aldous and Eagleson show that a martingale central limit theorem can be obtained directly using stability.

nl.statement:
At every even horizon \(T=2n\), the bounded two-regime score and randomization process of Proposition~\(\text{prop:endogenous-qv-self-normalization-obstruction}\) has an explicit bounded augmentation with a nondegenerate observable-outcome law and a nonzero causal effect that satisfies every assumption explicitly listed in Saco's Theorem~5.14 and also its maintained consistency and no-interference condition. Namely, let \((U_t)_{t=1}^T\) be independent Rademacher variables, independent of the action randomizers, set \(A_t^{\mathrm S}:=\mathbf1\{A_t=1\}\) and \(X_t^{\mathrm S}:=(X_t,U_t)\), and set
\[
 Y_t^{\mathrm S}(1)=\frac32+U_t,
 \qquad
 Y_t^{\mathrm S}(0)=\frac12+U_t.
\]
At context value \((x,u)\), set the predictable nuisance regressions to \(\widehat m_{t-1,1}(x,u)=u+1/2\) and \(\widehat m_{t-1,0}(x,u)=u-1/2\). Then the causal target is \(\theta_0=E_P[Y_t^{\mathrm S}(1)-Y_t^{\mathrm S}(0)]=1\), while the observed outcome obeys \(\operatorname{Var}(Y_t^{\mathrm S}\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})=1+p_t(1-p_t)\ge1\), where \(p_t:=P(A_t=1\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})\). Saco's centered AIPW increment is nevertheless exactly \(\xi_t\). Conditionally on \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\),
\[
 P\!\left(\xi_t=\frac1{p_t}\,\middle|\,\mathcal F_{t-1}\right)=p_t,
 \qquad
 P\!\left(\xi_t=-\frac1{1-p_t}\,\middle|\,\mathcal F_{t-1}\right)=1-p_t,
\]
and hence \(E(\xi_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})=0\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(\xi_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})=1/p_t+1/(1-p_t)\in\{4,16/3\}\). Saco's realized and predictable quadratic variations are therefore \(Q_T=[S]_T\) and \(V_T^2=\langle S\rangle_T\), with \(V_T^2\ge4T\) almost surely. Nevertheless, along \(T=2n\),
\[
 \frac{S_T}{\sqrt{Q_T}}\Longrightarrow
 L:=\mathbf1\{Z>0\}\frac{2Z+4W/\sqrt3}{\sqrt{28/3}}
 +\mathbf1\{Z\le0\}\frac{2Z+2W}{\sqrt8},
\]
where \(Z,W\) are independent \(N(0,1)\) variables and
\[
 E[L]=\frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi}}
 \left(\sqrt{\frac3{28}}-\frac1{\sqrt8}\right)\ne0.
\]
The feasible sample-variance Studentized AIPW statistic has the same limit \(L\). Thus the variance-growth-only normal-limit conclusions asserted in Saco's Theorem~5.14 are false as stated, even for bounded nondegenerate outcomes and a nonzero causal effect.

Remove hSaco and assert an existential carrying those construction identities and bounds together with ¬ SacoTheorem514Claim.

nl.statement:
Let \((X_{n,s},\mathcal G_{n,s})_{s=1}^{N_n}\) be a scalar martingale-difference triangular array, where \(N_n\to\infty\), and let \(0\le h_n<N_n\) be deterministic with \(h_n/N_n\to0\).  Suppose that for constants \(C_4<\infty\) and \(\lambda_->0\),
\[
\sup_{n,s}E|X_{n,s}|^4\le C_4,\qquad
\lambda_n\ge\lambda_-\quad\text{almost surely},
\]
where \(\lambda_n\) is positive and \(\mathcal G_{n,h_n}\)-measurable.  Define
\[
S_n=\sum_{s=1}^{N_n}X_{n,s},\qquad
Q_n=\sum_{s=1}^{N_n}X_{n,s}^2,\qquad
A_{n,+}^2=\sum_{s=h_n+1}^{N_n}E[X_{n,s}^2\mid\mathcal G_{n,s-1}].
\]
If \(A_{n,+}^2/(N_n\lambda_n)\to1\) in probability, then
\[
\frac{Q_n}{N_n\lambda_n}\longrightarrow1\quad\text{in probability},\qquad
P(Q_n>0)\longrightarrow1,\qquad
\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}\left|P\left\{\frac{S_n}{\sqrt{Q_n}}\le z\right\}-\Phi(z)\right|\longrightarrow0,
\]
where the ratio is set to zero on \(\{Q_n=0\}\).  Every conclusion is uniform over any collection of arrays for which \(C_4,\lambda_-\), \(h_n/N_n\to0\), and the displayed predictable-QV convergence are uniform.

review.note: After unfolding the array sums, predictable QV, martingale-difference, uniform-probability, uniform-event, and uniform-CDF predicates, the Lean hypotheses and all three uniform conclusions are equivalent to the paper statement; explicit fourth-power integrability supplies the finiteness presupposed by the displayed fourth moment.

nl.statement:
For the class in Definition~\(\mathrm{def:saco\text{-}early\text{-}stabilized\text{-}aipw\text{-}class}\), let \(S_n,Q_n,\widehat\theta_n,\widehat V_n,\theta_{0,n}\), and \(N_n=n_{\mathrm{eff}}\) have the meanings given there.  Then the centered AIPW scores are martingale differences in deterministic scored-set order, and there is a finite constant \(C_X\), depending only on the common overlap and outcome/nuisance fourth-moment envelopes, such that
\[
\sup_{n,\mathbb P_n,s}E_{\mathbb P_n}|X_{n,s}|^4\le C_X.
\]
For every \(\zeta>0\),
\[
\sup_{\mathbb P_n\in\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{Saco,es}}}
\mathbb P_n\left(\left|\frac{Q_n}{N_n\Lambda_n}-1\right|>\zeta\right)\longrightarrow0,
\]
and
\[
\sup_{\mathbb P_n\in\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{Saco,es}}}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
\left|\mathbb P_n\left\{\frac{S_n}{\sqrt{Q_n}}\le z\right\}-\Phi(z)\right|\longrightarrow0,
\]
where the score ratio is set to zero when \(Q_n=0\).  If
\[
Z_n^{\mathrm{feas}}=
\begin{cases}
\sqrt{N_n}(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_{0,n})/\sqrt{\widehat V_n},&\widehat V_n>0,\\
0,&\widehat V_n=0,
\end{cases}
\]
then
\[
\sup_{\mathbb P_n\in\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{Saco,es}}}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
\left|\mathbb P_n\{Z_n^{\mathrm{feas}}\le z\}-\Phi(z)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
Consequently, for every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), the interval
\[
\mathcal I_n(\alpha)=\left[\widehat\theta_n\ \pm\ \Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\sqrt{\widehat V_n/N_n}\right]
\]
satisfies
\[
\sup_{\mathbb P_n\in\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{Saco,es}}}
\left|\mathbb P_n\{\theta_{0,n}\in\mathcal I_n(\alpha)\}-(1-\alpha)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus the valid direct repair is Saco's published enumerated AIPW/DML class intersected with early measurable suffix-QV stabilization, not the variance-growth-only source class.

nl.statement:
In the bounded two-regime AIPW witness of Proposition~\(\mathrm{prop:saco\text{-}theorem\text{-}5\text{-}14\text{-}counterexample}\), at horizons \(T=2n\), no deterministic sequence \(k_T=o(T)\) and no positive \(\mathcal F_{k_T}\)-measurable scale \(\Lambda_T\), even if bounded uniformly away from zero, can satisfy
\[
\frac{\sum_{t=k_T+1}^{T}E[\xi_t^2\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]}{T\Lambda_T}\longrightarrow1
\quad\text{in probability}.
\]
Consequently the witness belongs to Saco's variance-growth-only hypothesis class but cannot belong to the early-stabilized class in Definition~\(\mathrm{def:saco\text{-}early\text{-}stabilized\text{-}aipw\text{-}class}\) for any cutoff \(k_T=o(n_{\mathrm{eff}})\).
